question: Question linked to image nº16 A 54-year-old black woman with asthenia, drowsiness, paresthesias, gait disorder, and loss of strength and sensation in both lower extremities. The analyzes showed Hb 10.4 g / dL, VCM 107 fL, platelets 110,000 / mm3, leukocytes 5,000 / mm3, neutrophils 1900 / mm3, lymphocytes 2500 / mm3, monocytes 300 / mm3, eosinophils 300 / mm3, reticulocytes 1.0% (normal: 0.5-2), total reticulocytes 5,400 / mm3, haptoglobin 0 g / L (normal 0.3-2 g / L), LDH 1,114 U / L, AST (GOT) 50 U / L, ALT ( GPT) 30 U / L, GGT 16 U / L, alkaline phosphatase 90 U / L, total bilirubin 1.03 mg / dL. Negative Coombs test. The peripheral blood smear is shown in the image. Assessed the clinical and analytical picture, what is the treatment that should be administered to this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Asthenia, drowsiness, paresthesias, gait disorder" -> "neurological symptoms" -> "possible vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "macrocytic anemia (MCV 107 fL)" -> "low haptoglobin, high LDH" -> "ineffective erythropoiesis" -> "parenteral vitamin B12" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Loss of strength and sensation in lower extremities" -> "neuropathy" -> "possible vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "macrocytic anemia" -> "low reticulocyte count" -> "high LDH, low haptoglobin" -> "parenteral vitamin B12" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Asthenia, drowsiness" -> "anemia symptoms" -> "macrocytic anemia" -> "low haptoglobin, high LDH" -> "hemolysis" -> "negative Coombs test" -> "parenteral vitamin B12" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Paresthesias, gait disorder" -> "neurological involvement" -> "possible vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "macrocytic anemia" -> "low haptoglobin, high LDH" -> "parenteral vitamin B12" -> 92%
CHAIN: "Hb 10.4 g/dL, MCV 107 fL" -> "macrocytic anemia" -> "neurological symptoms" -> "possible vitamin B12 deficiency" -> "low haptoglobin, high LDH" -> "parenteral vitamin B12" -> 88%
analysis: The patient presents with macrocytic anemia (MCV 107 fL), low haptoglobin, elevated LDH, and neurological symptoms such as paresthesias and gait disorder, which are indicative of vitamin B12 deficiency. The negative Coombs test and the presence of neurological symptoms further support this diagnosis. The treatment for vitamin B12 deficiency, especially with neurological involvement, is parenteral vitamin B12.
